title: Apple may have to officially support easy Apple Intelligence removal on Macs
snippet: You only have to read some of the comments right here to see that there’s a vocal minority of people rejecting all AI tools, including Apple Intelligence. That’s led to an unofficial tool enabling people to turn off the feature on their Macs and remove all downloaded Siri AI models. We warned yesterday that this could be a risky thing to do, but it’s now being suggested that Apple may have to officially support an AI removal feature in order to protect hardware sales … more…
fullText:
You only have to read some of the comments right here to see that there’s a vocal minority of people rejecting all AI tools, including Apple Intelligence. That’s led to an unofficial tool enabling people to turn off the feature on their Macs and remove all downloaded Siri AI models.

We warned yesterday that this could be a risky thing to do, but it’s now being suggested that Apple may have to officially support an AI removal feature in order to protect hardware sales …

There’s been growing pushback against generative AI in general, with opponents citing reasons ranging from fearing for the survival of the human species down to simply not wanting unwanted AI features to take up storage space on their devices.

The latest Apple Intelligence models can require up to 14GB of storage, so there’s a significant hit to 256GB machines if you don’t want the features. That led indie developer Om Lahore to create a project called RemoveMacAI.

	

We warned yesterday that using this is not without risks. Given how deeply Apple Intelligence is embedded into macOS 27, it could have unwanted impact on even quite basic functionality.

But some are arguing that Apple may have to introduce an official way to remove Apple Intelligence from Macs. Daring Fireball’s John Gruber points to organizations banning the installation of AI tools.

There are institutional groups that have rules against AI — these places aren’t allowing Golden Gate at all until and unless Apple Intelligence can be removed. And that means not buying new Mac hardware that only runs Golden Gate.

To be clear, Apple does offer a great many controls to organizations using device management. Currently, Apple says they can “restrict the use” of certain Apple Intelligence features, and there are individual toggles to enable or disable features one at a time. What’s currently lacking is a single switch to disable all Apple Intelligence features in one hit, together with the option to remove the downloaded models.

It’s not a live issue yet, but as future generations of Macs start dropping support for older versions of macOS, failing to allow the easy removal of AI models could start to hit Apple’s hardware sales.

title: Fitbit Edge is Google’s middle ground between Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch
snippet: Google’s newest wearable costs $179.99 and has a sleek feel like the Fitbit Air but with an OLED display.
fullText:
Google’s Fitbit lineup expanded on Monday with the introduction of the Fitbit Edge, a new wearable that’s positioned between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch. 

Priced at $179.99, it combines the Fitbit Air’s slim band with an OLED display for checking map directions, notifications, weather, and music controls. 

Like the Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air, the Edge works with Google Health Coach, powered by Gemini. (You’ll need a Google Health Premium subscription to use it.) The coach can use your fitness, health, and medical information to put together weekly routines and workout plans, then adjust them around your schedule.

It also comes with Google’s Health Guardian feature, which is designed to spot notable changes in health measurements over time, including indicators related to blood pressure and insulin resistance. (The company announced these features at the Pixel Watch 5 launch in August.)

Image Credits:Google

Google says the Fitbit Edge can automatically recognize and log up to 100 activities, including runs, bike rides, and walks. The company explains it uses context from your movement to work out what you’re doing and add it to your weekly goals. Plus, the device supports more than 50 exercise modes and can offer on-screen prompts during workouts, such as a nudge to push harder or take a breather.

The Fitbit Edge’s built-in GPS is 40% more accurate than the previous generation, the company claims, which should make it easier to track outdoor runs. Google says sleep-stage detection is also 15% more accurate than on earlier generations, helping the device provide better sleep summaries and coaching tips.

Meanwhile, the battery is rated for up to seven days on a charge, and the wearable is water-resistant to 50 meters.

The Fitbit Edge is available to preorder through the Google Store, with store availability set for October 27.

Color choices include Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon. There’s also a Stephen Curry Special Edition, priced at $219.99.

title: iOS 27.2 release date: When to expect new iPhone features
snippet: iOS 27.2 is coming surprisingly soon. iOS 27.1 will focus on iPhone Duo changes only, so new features for everyone else will arrive in iOS 27.2. Here’s when to expect the update’s release. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.2 is coming surprisingly soon. iOS 27.1 will focus on iPhone Duo changes only, so new features for everyone else will arrive in iOS 27.2. Here’s when to expect the update’s release.

iOS 27.2 confirmed to launch in October, likely late in the month

Apple is currently beta testing iOS 27.2, and has been for several weeks now. It’s being tested much sooner than a x.2 release normally would, but for good reason.

iPhone Duo launches October 23 running iOS 27.1. And all indications are that no other iPhones will get that update, instead jumping straight to 27.2.

By keeping iOS 27.1 exclusive to iPhone Duo, Apple can keep more details of the software experience under wraps by not potentially exposing them during a beta process. That’s why iOS 27.2 is currently in beta instead.

When will iOS 27.2 launch? We know it is coming in October.

Last month when iOS 27 debuted, Apple said that Siri AI would add support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish “next month.”

Those new Siri languages are included in iOS 27.2, thus confirming an October release. Additional new features coming with iOS 27.2 include:

user profiles in the Apple TV app

Dual Capture for Group FaceTime

new Suggestions feature in Messages

Up Next overhaul for Apple Podcasts

design updates for Apple Books

Historically, Apple has shipped its first feature update after a major new OS version in late October, and that’s what we’re expecting this year too. The week of October 26 is the most likely launch window.

iOS 27.2 could always arrive slightly sooner, especially if new hardware introduced next week ships with it pre-installed. But the rumored Home products likely won’t ship right away. Instead, the first orders could deliver during that final week in October, right when iOS 27.2, tvOS 27.2, and HomePod 27.2 all ship too.

title: No Man’s Sky is coming to the iPhone and iPad
snippet: The No Man's Sky universe is about to get a little bit smaller - but in a good way. Hello Games announced that its long-running sci-fi exploration game will be coming to iOS, with versions for both the iPhone and iPad available starting on October 28th. According to Hello's Sean Murray, the mobile version of the game is essentially the full No Man's Sky experience. "I guess I should say this is not No Man's Sky Lite," he wrote in a blog post. It includes all of the game's many, many updates that have come out since launch - like the gigantic Voyagers expansion from last year - and the only major features missing will be multiplayer and the … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Andrew Webster

 

is an entertainment editor covering streaming, virtual worlds, and every single Pokémon video game. Andrew joined The Verge in 2012, writing over 4,000 stories.

The No Man’s Sky universe is about to get a little bit smaller — but in a good way. Hello Games announced that its long-running sci-fi exploration game will be coming to iOS, with versions for both the iPhone and iPad available starting on October 28th.

According to Hello’s Sean Murray, the mobile version of the game is essentially the full No Man’s Sky experience. “I guess I should say this is not No Man’s Sky Lite,” he wrote in a blog post. It includes all of the game’s many, many updates that have come out since launch — like the gigantic Voyagers expansion from last year — and the only major features missing will be multiplayer and the planetary settlements. Murray likens the iOS version to when the game initially launched on the original Switch. “On Switch we have listened to players and built from there, including with a much expanded version on Switch 2,” he says. “Based on feedback and player numbers we will support iOS in a similar way.”

The game will be playable on the iPhone 11 and 3rd generation iPad Air and above, and the studio says that the download comes in at a surprisingly scant 5GB. It also has newly-designed touch controls, as well as support for controllers, screen casting, and mouse-and-keyboard on the iPad. Murray also notes that “Perhaps most importantly we’ve put tons of work into battery life and thermodynamics, and we’re super proud that No Man’s Sky can be enjoyed for really long comfortable play sessions.” It’ll be “free to try” at launch, though it’s not clear how much the full version will cost.

It’s now been a decade since No Man’s Sky first launched, and the game has changed dramatically since its debut. iOS will be joining a huge list of supported platforms, including Mac, PC, and essentially every modern console, and there’s also a VR version available. Just as significant, Hello has continued to keep the game vibrant with a constant stream of free expansions, including the recent Cosmos update in September, which fleshed out the vast expanse of space with more things to explore.

fullText:
Dominic Preston

 

is a news editor with over a decade’s experience in journalism. He previously worked at Android Police and Tech Advisor.

Today the OnePlus 16 launched in China, the company’s first flagship phone since quitting both the US and European markets this summer. As luck would have it, it also looks like the company’s best phone in some time.

Like most OnePlus phones, the 16 is positioned around performance, with a Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset, and up to 1TB of storage and 16GB of RAM. That’s backed up by an enormous 9,000mAh silicon-carbon battery, one of the biggest seen in any Android flagship yet. 100W wired and 50W wireless charging complete the power setup.

On the display front, the phone jumps to a 185Hz OLED panel for the first time. That’ll not only be used for 185fps gaming in compatible titles, but can also run at up to 165Hz throughout the system UI — a first for high refresh rate panels like this.

Image: OnePlus

Even the cameras, not usually OnePlus’ strong suit, have had a meaningful upgrade. The main camera has a higher resolution (200 megapixels), larger sensor (1/1.4-inch-type), and faster aperture (f/1.4) than the OnePlus 15’s. That should help, given we found that phone’s camera had frustrating “imitations in low light.” 50-megapixel ultrawide and telephoto cameras round out the rear trio, and the latter also enjoys a big bump to a 1/1.95-inch sensor.

Image: OnePlus

There’s a design flourish too, with the phone’s silver finish including LED lighting that features a big “16” and what the company claims is a set of galactic coordinates. While the shapes of the lights are fixed, they’ll reportedly flash with different rhythms to notify you of calls, messages, battery level, and more.

The OnePlus 16 is available in China starting from ¥5,699 (about $850). With OnePlus no longer in either the US or Europe, there’s no hope of a launch for the 16 in either market.

title: Apple TV just unveiled the new season of last year’s hit comedy
snippet: One of Apple TV’s hit comedy series from last year, Stick, is coming back for season 2 soon. Here’s the new trailer for Stick’s highly anticipated return. more…
fullText:
One of Apple TV’s hit comedy series from last year, Stick, is coming back for season 2 soon. Here’s the new trailer for Stick’s highly anticipated return.

Stick season 2 is coming November 4, here’s the trailer

Ted Lasso just wrapped up its fourth season, but Apple TV has another heartfelt sports comedy ready to take its place.

Stick returns for season 2 on Wednesday, November 4, with two episodes available initially then weekly releases through December 30.

Watch Stick on Apple TV

For the unfamiliar, Stick stars Owen Wilson as an ex-pro golfer—Pryce Cahill—whose career ended prematurely. But after helping train a 17-year-old golf phenom in season 1, the new season sees Cahill get back to the game himself.

And he’ll do it with the help of a new coach played by Rhea Seehorn (“Pluribus”).

Here’s Apple’s official season summary, followed by the new trailer:

In season two, Santi takes the next step in his pursuit of professional golf, only to discover how quickly the game changes when talent becomes expectation. As Santi chases his dream, Pryce finds himself wondering what might still be possible for him. Urged on by his former rival Clark Ross (Timothy Olyphant), Pryce does something nobody expects: he bets on himself, launching an improbable comeback in hopes of becoming the oldest golfer ever to win a major. But the road back proves far harder than he imagined. And the closer Pryce gets to the golfer he once was, the more he is forced to confront why he never fulfilled the promise everyone once saw in him. With brilliant new coach Amanda (Rhea Seehorn) and trusted caddie Mitts (Marc Maron) in his corner, Pryce sets out to prove — to the golf world and, more importantly, to himself — that maybe he really was as good as everyone always said he was.

In my experience, you don’t have to care about golf at all to enjoy Stick.

The show feels similar in spirit to other Apple comedies like Ted Lasso and Shrinking. In my view it especially hit its stride near the end of the season, so I’m excited to see it return.

If you’re looking for more Apple series to check out, Small Prophets just premiered and is being hailed as a “masterpiece” and in contention for the streamer’s best show this year.

Are you a fan of Stick? Or do you plan to watch it ahead of season 2? Let us know in the comments.

title: Googlebook gets Luminar photo editing app with ‘Continue On’ support
snippet: One of the biggest questions around Googlebook is what app support will look like and, as the platform officially arrives for customers this week, Luminar is debuting a rebuilt photo editing app for Googlebook. more…
fullText:
One of the biggest questions around Googlebook is what app support will look like and, as the platform officially arrives for customers this week, Luminar is debuting a rebuilt photo editing app for Googlebook.

Luminar is a photo editing app that’s available across desktop platforms like Mac and Windows, but it’s also on Android, iOS, iPad, and ChromeOS. Now, it’s also making the jump to Googlebook.

The Luminar app has been rebuilt with support for Googlebok OS and meets “Tier 1” quality standards for the platform including keyboard shortcuts, resizable windows, drag-and-drop, and more. 

That’s on top of Luminar’s existing Android support for photo editing which includes the ability to adjust qualities of your photo, handle RAW edits, and use AI for features such as swapping out a background, masking, and more. You can even start edits on your phone and finish on your Googlebook as Luminar supports “Continue On.”

	

Luminar explains in a press release:

Luminar for Googlebook is fully adapted for large screens, meeting Google’s Tier 1 quality standards and introducing capabilities such as drag-and-drop, keyboard shortcuts, and resizable windows that weren’t previously available on phones and tablets. After several rounds of testing, Luminar has built a range of capabilities specifically for Googlebook OS:  

Built for the laptop: resizable windows, full mouse and keyboard support, shortcuts, hover states, multitasking, drag and drop, and file handling

New for launch: Generative Erase, HDR Merge, and batch editing – features usually associated with professional editing

One app, one subscription: use Luminar on an Android phone and on a Googlebook with the same account. [If available at launch:] With Continue On, you can start an edit on your phone and finish it on the laptop

Googlebook owners can download Lunimar via the Play Store. A temporary offer gives 12 months of access to Luminar for free, with a later one-time purchase unlocking the app’s premium features permanently.

title: Google announces $179 Fitbit Edge tracker with display, GPS
snippet: Google is following the Fitbit Air launched in May with a second tracker that features a screen called the Fitbit Edge. more…
fullText:
Google is following the Fitbit Air launched in May with a second tracker that features a screen called the Fitbit Edge.

The Fitbit Edge features a wide, pill-shaped AMOLED screen — protected by Gorilla Glass 3 — that offers 46% more display than the Charge 6 from 2023. The 11.5mm-thick body is made from precision-crafted aluminum with nano-molding technology to allow for a 40% more precise GPS (versus Charge 6), while there’s a dedicated altimeter for elevation tracking. On the right side, you’ll find a large button for tactile control, like when swimming. This device has IP68 / 5ATM dust and water protection.

On the underside, you’ll find the sensors. The Fitbit Edge has an accelerometer, altimeter, ambient light sensor, far-field skin temperature sensor, gyroscope, heart rate sensor, multipurpose electrical sensors (ECG), and red and infrared sensors (SpO2).

The Fitbit Edge uses the same magnetic USB-C charger as the Fitbit Air. A 5-minute charge gives you a day of battery, while a full top-up takes 90 minutes. Battery life is rated at a week with the always-on display disabled. When enabled, the Fitbit Edge comes in at around 2 days. Like the Pixel Watch 5, you can open the device to replace the battery.

	

The Fitbit Edge is available in the following colors:

Matte Black Aluminum case / Obsidian Active Band

Polished Silver Aluminum case / Fog Active Band

Satin Pyrite Aluminum case / Olive Active Band

Champagne Gold case / Canyon Active Band

The bands are replaceable with a new swap mechanism and four additional designs: 

$39.99 Active Sport: Made of “ultra soft silicone” with large pill-shaped cutouts

$59.99 Magnet Band: Clasp-free design with magnets embedded into the strap

$149.99 Metal Links

$49.99 Performance Loop: Stretch and micro-adjustable

Supporting Android and iOS, the Edge is running a Fitbit operating system similar to the Air. A larger screen unlocks a richer interface that takes inspiration from the Pixel Watch 5.

Google showed a dozen or so watch faces for the Fitbit Edge with analog and digital options. You can customize what complications appear via the Google Health app.

Swiping left/right from the watch face lets you access various tiles, with the order customizable. This includes Quick start (for different exercises), Focus metrics, Sleep, Heart, Cycle health, Weather, Timers, Alarms, and Music controls.

Compared to the Charge 6, music controls work with any app on your paired device, while phone notifications are also available. Quick replies to messages are limited to Android due to iOS platform limitations. You also get Google Maps navigation, but there is no Google Wallet given the lack of NFC.

	

The Exercise app lets you track over 50 types of activity with real-time guidance and workout views. The Fitbit Edge can connect to equipment with heart rate broadcasting. 

The Fitbit Edge (and the Air) feature upgraded automatic activity detection. This AI-powered contextual reasoning can learn your habits over time to add support for over 100 activities. 

You can have the Fitbit Air, Edge, and Pixel Watch 5 operate on the same account with seamless switching.

The Fitbit Edge costs $179.99 with pre-orders open today and availability on October 27. A Stephen Curry Special Edition is available for $219.99 with a custom band.

title: iPhone Air 2 is coming, here’s everything we know so far
snippet: Apple is working on a second-generation iPhone Air, and it could address several key limitations of the current model. Here’s everything we know about the iPhone Air 2, including features, release date, and more. more…
fullText:
Apple is working on a second-generation iPhone Air, and it could address several key limitations of the current model. Here’s everything we know about the iPhone Air 2, including features, release date, and more.

Will there be an iPhone Air 2?

The iPhone Air has reportedly sold worse than Apple expected. The Information reported in November that Apple had indefinitely delayed the release of a second-generation model due to those lower-than-expected sales.

Apple reportedly “notified engineers and suppliers that they were taking the next iPhone Air off the schedule without providing a new release date.”

Shortly thereafter, however, The Information updated its reporting to say Apple wasn’t canceling the iPhone Air 2 altogether and that one is still very much in the works.

iPhone Air 2 features

A second camera

One of the biggest tradeoffs of the ultra-thin iPhone Air design is that it only has one camera. This is reportedly something Apple is pushing to change for the iPhone Air 2.

According to sources including Bloomberg and The Information, the iPhone Air 2 will have a second camera on the back.

Bloomberg says it will be an ultra-wide camera, not a telephoto camera. This would align it with Apple’s base model iPhones, which also have a main camera and an ultra-wide camera.

A20 Pro chip

The iPhone Air 2 will reportedly be powered by the A20 Pro processor, up from the A19 Pro in the current model.

The A20 Pro chip will be Apple’s first 2-nanometer iPhone processor. This new fabrication process will mean the A20 Pro can offer more power and be more efficient in a similar-sized footprint.

The chip will also use another new innovation called Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module, which integrates the SoC and DRAM at the wafer level for better performance and lower power consumption.

Better battery life

Apple is also reportedly working to improve the battery life of the iPhone Air 2.

According to a supply chain leak, the iPhone Air 2 will have a 3,500mAh battery. For comparison’s sake, the first-generation iPhone Air has a 3,149mAh battery, so this is an increase of more than 10%.

Beyond increasing the physical size of the battery, the iPhone Air 2 will likely offer longer battery life thanks to the efficiency improvements of the A20 Pro chip.

It’s important to remember, however, that there are many variables at play when it comes to an iPhone’s battery life. We’ll have to wait and see the exact numbers when Apple officially unveils the iPhone Air 2.

Vapor chamber

According to The Information, the iPhone Air 2 will feature a vapor chamber cooling system. Apple first debuted its vapor chamber cooling technology in the iPhone 17 Pro, touting significantly improved heat dissipation and performance.

If Apple brings the vapor chamber to the iPhone Air 2, it means the device will stay cooler during high workloads and sustain high performance for longer periods.

iPhone Air 2: Release date

The iPhone Air 2 was originally expected to be released in September 2026 alongside the iPhone 18 Pro lineup.

Most recently, however, Bloomberg reported that Apple plans to release the iPhone Air 2 in spring 2027 alongside the new base model iPhone 18.

title: Apple Mail added four convenient new features in iOS 27
snippet: iOS 27 brings new features to Apple Wallet, Maps, Notes, Messages, and more—and it packs key upgrades for the Mail app too. Here’s everything new for Apple Mail in iOS 27. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 brings new features to Apple Wallet, Maps, Notes, Messages, and more—and it packs key upgrades for the Mail app too. Here’s everything new for Apple Mail in iOS 27.

Upgraded search

If you have much history using Apple Mail, you’ll know that its search feature hasn’t always been the best. But in iOS 27, search has gotten a big upgrade.

From Apple’s website:

More relevant search in Mail. A new ranking system brings the most relevant results to the top to help you find what you need right away — even if it’s buried deep in your inbox.

I can’t count the number of times search has previously failed to find messages that I knew existed. So far in my testing, iOS 27 seems to have fixed that.

New suggestions that include third-party apps

Suggestions at the top of messages have been in Apple Mail for years. But in iOS 27, they get a new, more flexible design and expand to support third-party apps.

When Mail detects that you might want to take action on the contents of an email, a suggestion might appear at the top of the message. These include: directions in Maps, creating events in Calendar, tracking a shipment with Apple Wallet, and more.

In iOS 27, third-party apps can offer suggestions too. And when multiple apps are available with suggested actions, there’s a drop-down menu to show you all available options.

Smart Reply improvements

Smart Reply is a keyboard feature that automatically surfaces reply options you can utilize with a single tap.

In iOS 27, the next generation of Apple Intelligence comes with improvements to Smart Reply.

Apple says that Smart Reply “can now draw on a user’s personalized writing style.” Essentially, rather than offering fairly generic reply options, now Smart Reply suggestions will actually sound a lot more like you.

Siri AI capabilities

Apple has added ‘Ask Siri’ buttons throughout Apple Mail, just like the rest of its system apps. And Siri AI brings a bunch of new powers for Mail users.

One example I’ve seen several times on social media already is that you can ask Siri to delete all messages from a specific sender that’s spamming you.

Bug fixes

Beyond new features, Apple also says that iOS 27 makes the Mail app run better than ever thanks to bug fixes and performance improvements. Here are some specific examples given:

Faster message loading in Mail

More reliable search indexing in Mail

Improved list formatting in Mail

Improved unread badge accuracy in Mail

title: How to Disable Some Apple Intelligence Features on Your iPhone or Mac and Reclaim Valuable Space
snippet: The new AI features could be taking up a lot of storage on your device.
fullText:
Apple launched iOS 27 and MacOS 27 in September, and those updates introduced a revamped Siri AI powered by Apple Intelligence to Apple devices. While the new Siri was better at most tasks in my testing, it can still take up a significant amount of on-device storage space. On my iPhone, for example, it takes up about 6.4GB of data, while it takes up about 17.9GB of space on my MacBook Neo.

If you aren’t using the new AI features, you can disable some of them, and depending on what system you’re on, you can reclaim some of that valuable storage space. That way you can stave off for a little while the dreaded pop-up that tells you your storage is full – I need that extra storage for photos of my wife, son and dog.

		

			

Here’s how to see how much storage Apple Intelligence is taking up on your devices and how to disable – or at least limit – it on different operating systems. And don’t forget, Apple Intelligence is only available on certain devices.

How much space is Apple Intelligence taking up on your device?

How much space Apple Intelligence is taking up on your device is easy to check. If you’re on iPhone, go to Settings > General > iPhone Storage > iOS. From here, look for the Apple Intelligence tab to see how much space it takes up on your iPhone.

On a MacBook, click the Apple logo in the top-left corner of your screen, then go to System Settings > General > Storage, and click the i next to MacOS. A new pop-up will open to show you how much space Apple Intelligence uses on your MacBook.

Disabling Apple Intelligence on your iPhone that’s running iOS 27 or later is straightforward. Go to Settings > Siri > Turn Off Siri and follow the on-screen prompts. You can then go back and check your storage, and Apple Intelligence should be gone from that menu.

Disabling Siri AI can free up a few gigabytes on iOS 27.CNET

If you’re running iOS 26, you can disable Apple Intelligence by going to Settings > Apple Intelligence & Siri and tapping the toggle next to Apple Intelligence. This should free up some space on your iPhone.

You might also have to disable other Apple Intelligence features across your iPhone. To do this, go to Settings > Screen Time > Content & Privacy Restrictions and tap the toggle next to Content & Privacy Restrictions. Then, tap Intelligence & Siri. From here, you’ll need to tap into Image Creation, Writing Tools and Intelligence Extensions and tap Don’t Allow in each one.

This should free up a few gigabytes of space on your iPhone.

You can free up a few gigabytes of space in iOS 26 by disabling Apple Intelligence features.CNET

How to disable Apple Intelligence on your Mac

Disabling Apple Intelligence and freeing up storage space on your device can be weird, depending on which operating system you’re using. For instance, if you’re on MacOS 26, it’s easy to disable the feature and free up space. If you’re on MacOS 27, it’s a little more complicated. 

We’ll start off with the easy one. To disable Apple Intelligence on MacOS 26, first click the Apple logo in the top left corner of your screen. Then go to System Settings > Apple Intelligence & Siri and click to toggle next to Apple Intelligence. That should free up a few gigabytes of data on your device.

Disabling Apple Intelligence on MacOS 26 frees up a little bit of storage.CNET

There are a couple of potential ways to disable Apple Intelligence on MacOS 27. The easiest way I found to free up a few gigabytes of space is to click the Apple logo in the top-left corner of your screen, then go to System Settings > Siri and change your language to something like English (Irish). Siri AI isn’t available in every region yet, so changing your Siri language to a language from one of those regions could trick your device. Granted, it freed up only about 4 GB for me.

I changed my Siri language, and it freed up a few gigabytes of space.CNET

CNET’s sister site PCMag has a more in-depth way of turning off Apple Intelligence and freeing up some space. However, I couldn’t get this method to work. I’m not sure why I couldn’t get this method to work, other than that my device is running MacOS 27.0.1 and not MacOS 27. Maybe this will work for you, though.

According to PCMag, you have to go to System Settings > Screen Time > Content & Privacy. Then, toggle Content & Privacy off. Click Siri and change it to Siri Classic. Then go through the list of Capabilities and turn each feature off.

You’re not finished yet. Then, go to System Settings > Siri and select Don’t Allow Siri or Siri Classic.

Finally, you’ll need to go into individual Apple Intelligence settings and disable those features. Some easy ones include going to System Settings > Notifications > Summarize Notifications and turning the toggle off, or going to System Settings > Messages > Settings and turning off Message Summaries.

You could do all that work, or you could just switch your Siri language as I did. The choice is yours.

For more iOS news, here’s what to know about iOS 27 and iOS 27.0.1.

title: The Beautiful Blue Is My Favorite Thing About Vivo’s Foldable X Fold 6
snippet: It’s a solid example of an Android foldable, but I worry that Apple has changed the game.
fullText:
Having spent a few days with Vivo’s new foldable X Fold 6, I can say there’s plenty I like about it, from its solid camera performance to its extremely good battery life. But because I’m shallow and like pretty things, I have to admit that its vibrant blue design with frosted glass back is my favorite thing about this phone. 

It’s by no means the first foldable I’ve liked based on looks alone — Oppo’s Find N6 won me over with its punchy orange color and, like the Oppo, Vivo’s foldable is tough to get hold of. It’s not officially sold in either the US or the UK, and while it’s possible to import these phones from resellers in China or the few parts of Europe where it is sold, I don’t recommend doing so as you’ll be left with no customer support should anything go wrong. 

I really love that lovely blue tone. It’s delightful.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

The X Fold 6 is a typical book-style foldable, akin to the Oppo Find N6 or Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. I wonder how much longer we’ll see this format of foldable now that Apple has launched its iPhone Duo with its stumpy “passport” dimensions. Samsung’s Z Fold 8 has the same proportions — as does Xiaomi’s 18 Fold that I saw at IFA 2026 — and it’s clearly becoming the fashionable way to make a folding phone, thanks to its wider internal dimensions that are better for watching videos than the square-format inner screens on the X Fold 6 and others.

			

More from CNET

This more “traditional” format still has its merits, and Vivo’s new model is a good example. It feels sturdy, and while it’s not as skinny when closed as Samsung’s Z Fold 8 Ultra or Oppo’s Find N6, it’s still svelte enough to slide into a pocket without much issue. It runs last year’s MediaTek Dimensity 9500 processor, which produced decent scores on our benchmark tests, and gaming and multitasking were absolutely no problem here. 

It’s an impressive camera setup for a foldable phone.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

The rear cameras are capable of taking some great-looking shots, thanks in part to the 200 megapixel sensor with high quality Zeiss glass in front of it. I don’t love that there are Vivo watermarks on by default (which I had to crop out of these examples — I subsequently turned off watermarks in the settings). But the main, ultrawide and telephoto cameras can take good photos.

This complex harbor scene was handled extremely well by the main camera.Andrew Lanxon/CNET
The highlights are a little bright here, but I love the authentic color tones.Andrew Lanxon/CNET
When viewed at full screen, this image from the telephoto zoom camera looks pretty decent, with a solid exposure and great colors.Andrew Lanxon/CNET
But cropping into 100% shows that there’s a lot of software processing going on, resulting in the fine details looking very… weird. It’s fine for an Instagram post, but little else.Andrew Lanxon/CNET
There’s a variety of filmic color presets to play with if you fancy getting a bit creative with your photography.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

The camera heavily relies on AI-based image processing in the longer focal lengths, resulting in fine details looking more like watercolor paintings, but that’s par for the course for most phones these days. Overall, though, I think the Vivo does a solid job with its cameras, especially for a foldable phone, which typically have watered-down versions of the camera setups from regular phones. This one feels like less of a compromise.

Where it seems to really shine though is battery life. After an hour of streaming YouTube on its massive inner screen at max brightness, it had dropped from full to… well, it was still full. It hadn’t dropped a single percent and only dropped to 94% after the second hour. That’s up there with the absolute best we’ve tested this year, including the iPhone 18 Pro. 

The crease isn’t invisible, but it’s not especially obvious either. A fair effort.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

Needless to say, getting through at least a full day of mixed use with the X Fold 6 should be no problem at all, and you probably won’t struggle to get most of the way into the second, as long as you’re careful with what you do.

Need to get some more juice in quickly? No problem, as its 80-watt wired charging means it’ll go from empty to full in around 30 minutes, so long as you have a compatible charger. 

The X Fold 6 isn’t breaking any boundaries among foldables — it’s not the slimmest or the most powerful, nor does it have the least visible crease — but it’s a great example of a phone that ticks every box you’d expect from a high-end device. What’s a real shame is that almost none of you reading this will be able to buy it. Sad face.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Andrew Lanxon
						

						

							Editor at Large; Lead Photographer, Europe						
					

											

								

											When he's not testing the latest phones or phone cameras, Andrew can normally be found with his own camera in hand or behind his drums or eating his stash of home-cooked food -- sometimes all at once.

title: Hands-on: Sonos Ace Ultra fix nearly everything I wanted from the original [Video]
snippet: I have been a huge Sonos fan and customer for years, dating back to the original Sonos One. So, about two years ago, when I heard that Sonos was entering the over-ear headphone market, I knew I had to give it a try. The Sonos Ace looked great, was very comfortable, and brought some cool Sonos ecosystem features. But for a premium pair of headphones, there were still a few areas that left me wanting more, like strong bass, better ANC, and a better app experience. So I have a good grasp on them now, and here is what you need to know. more…
fullText:
I have been a huge Sonos fan and customer for years, dating back to the original Sonos One. So, about two years ago, when I heard that Sonos was entering the over-ear headphone market, I knew I had to give it a try. The Sonos Ace looked great, was very comfortable, and brought some cool Sonos ecosystem features. But for a premium pair of headphones, there were still a few areas that left me wanting more, like strong bass, better ANC, and a better app experience. But now, the new Sonos Ace Ultra feels like they went down that list and addressed nearly every complaint that most customers had, including me. I have been using them as my main headphones for almost a month now, for travel, video editing, workouts, walks, and everyday listening. So I have a good grasp on them now, and here is what you need to know.

Be sure to check out our hands-on video review for the Sonos Ace Ultra below:

Sonos Ace Ultra

At first glance, the Sonos Ace Ultra does not look much different from the original Sonos Ace. They decided to keep the same clean, understated design with a few differently placed chrome accents and some additional colors. But the biggest differences are inside these headphones. 

What’s new versus the original Sonos Ace

Here are some of the biggest changes from the original Sonos Ace to the Ace Ultra:

Redesigned 40mm drivers

10-microphone array, up from eight mics on the original

Improved adaptive ANC, stating up to 2X more effective and being able to adjust to things like glasses, hair, and changes in the seal around your ears

Longer battery life with up to 35 hours with ANC turned on

Bluetooth 6.0 versus 5.4 on the older generation

Expanded EQ controls with three and an advanced eight-band EQ options

Headphones linking with the Sonos Ecosystem

User-replaceable batteries

Updated ear and headband cushion materials  

More rotation of the ear cups so they can sit flat when around your neck

Two new colors: Agave and Sand

The main things that I noticed in these changes are the redesigned acoustics, better bass response, and stronger ANC. With the original Sonos Ace, I would sometimes get this hissing noise when I was in ANC mode. This would rarely happen, but I did notice it. So far, the new Sonos Ace Ultra has alleviated that issue. You also still get some of the great specs from the previous model like:

Spatial audio and Dolby Atmos

Dynamic head tracking

Lossless audio on supported devices

USB-C and 3.5mm wired audio support

Bluetooth multipoint

Fast charging with up to three hours of playback from a three-minute charge

TV Audio Swap with compatible Sonos soundbars

They still have the same super high-quality design, combining plastics and metals to give you a premium, lightweight feel. The Sonos Ace Ultra also keeps the magnetically replaceable ear cups, and one of the best things that I have noticed is the new EQ settings that really let me hone in on how I like to listen to my music. But how were they as an everyday pair of headphones?

My experience

Again, it’s easy to put specs on paper, but the biggest reason I’ve enjoyed the Ace Ultras is that they actually sound noticeably better. My biggest complaint about the original Sonos Ace was the lack of bass depth. The bass was not bad, but for a pair of $450 headphones, I felt like they were lacking a bit. I listen to a lot of R&B, hip-hop, and pop music, so bass is important to me. I wanted more low-end impact and to feel the bass. The Ace Ultra finally delivers the experience that I wanted. 

There is substantially more punch and depth at the low end. But one thing to note here is that Sonos hasn’t achieved that by simply turning up the bass slider. Any headphone brand can crank up the bass, but the difficult part is maintaining separation so that the bass doesn’t overwhelm the vocals, instruments, and higher-end frequencies. That is where the Ace Ultra has really impressed me. The bass hits harder, but the vocals are still clear, crisp, and easy to listen to. And it’s not just for music; all media sounds better, like podcasts, movies, and all the YouTube videos I watch. They have sounded fantastic in all media listening situations. 

The improved ANC is something else I noticed immediately. The new 10 mic array allows even more sound to be dynamically pushed away from the headphones. Even when there is no media playing, it’s insane how quiet the headphones are in so many different environments. It’s almost too good! The biggest improvement to ANC is the unpredictable noises. It’s one thing to block out a consistent noise like an airplane engine, but another to block out passing cars, construction, sirens, or sudden loud sounds while walking outside.

Two final things I want to bring up are comfort and the Sonos ecosystem. These headphones are the most comfortable headphones I have worn. Even on a long 8-10-hour airplane ride, I wore them 95% of the time, and I felt no aches, pain, or heat at all. Lastly, I have a lot of Sonos speakers around my house, and they introduced a new feature that lets you move music from a speaker to your headphones with the press of a button. It’s a very cool feature, but I personally haven’t used it much.

My only complaint is that they need a new zipper or mechanism for the headphone case because that sticker gets stuck way too often!

Pricing and availability 

The Sonos Ace Ultra is available today on Sonos’s site and Amazon for $449, keeping the same launch price as the original Sonos Ace. They come in four colors: Black, White, Agave, and Sand. I also noticed that the original Sonos Ace is available on Amazon for $239 while supplies last. At $240, now that could be a good choice as well.

At $450, the Sonos Ace Ultra is firmly in the premium noise-canceling headphone category alongside options from Apple, Bose, and Sony.

Final take

The original Sonos Ace felt like a good first-generation product. The Sonos Ace Ultra feels like a complete and finished product. As we saw, they did not reinvent the look or design, but they improved in all the areas that mattered and even added a few new cool features. The sound is noticeably better, the ANC is strong and smarter, battery life lasts longer, the app experience is smoother, and that Agave color is amazing.

If you already own the OG Sonos Ace, I actually think there is enough here to justify the upgrade, depending on what you value. If you are in the market for a premium set of headphones, I think the Sonos Ace Ultra needs to be on your shortlist. At $449, they are certainly not cheap, but if you want one of the best premium headphones and are a Sonos fan, then you will love these.

title: Redesigned MacBook Pro will reportedly include these three changes
snippet: Apple has a fully redesigned MacBook Pro launching soon, its first new design since 2021. Here are three design changes reportedly coming. more…
fullText:
Apple has a fully redesigned MacBook Pro launching soon, its first new design since 2021. Here are three design changes reportedly coming.

#1: No notch

One of the defining traits of the current MacBook Pro design is its display cutout: the notch.

The MacBook Pro introduced the notch to the Mac line in 2021, and the redesigned model that’s about to launch will reportedly remove it. Instead, the new MacBook Pro will have a small camera cutout and Dynamic Island built in. Per Mark Gurman:

The Dynamic Island on the Mac will be built around a hole-punch-sized cutout for the computer’s camera. It’s smaller than the pill-shaped notch in current iPhones.

It sounds like the notch replacement could be similar to iPhone Duo’s hole-punch camera on its outer display.

#2: Thinner and lighter

The current MacBook Pro is a hefty powerhouse, but Apple reportedly has a thinner, lighter design coming for the new MacBook Pro. Per Bloomberg earlier this week:

The new MacBook Pros are lighter — significantly lighter. Apple has reengineered the machine’s interior miniaturizing parts and rearranging components to make the computer much easier to carry.

It’s unknown whether slimming the MacBook Pro will result in any ports being removed. Apple’s current MacBook Pro design brought back many ports that had been removed in the prior iteration. It would be surprising for the company to strip ports yet again.

#3: Slightly larger displays

An Omdia report this summer said the redesigned MacBook Pro will come in two screen sizes:

14.3 inches

16.3 inches

	

If accurate, this is a very slight increase over the current 14.2- and 16.2-inch sizes. It’s possible Apple will reduce the bezels a bit to achieve a larger usable display area.

It’s also possible that the overall form factor will get slightly larger to help provide extra space for components despite the thinner body. But there are no specific rumors around these details yet.

title: Move Over ‘Carrie’: Mike Flanagan Teases ‘The Exorcist: Martyrs’ at NYCC 2026
snippet: The prolific horror filmmaker unveiled the trailer for The Exorcist: Martyrs, which he said is “the scariest movie” he’s ever made.
fullText:
Mike Flanagan is a busy man. Just this week, his TV series remake of Stephen King‘s horror classic, Carrie, premiered on Prime Video. Clayface, the body-horror movie inspired by the DC Comics character, for which he cowrote the script, hits theaters on Oct. 23.

Now, he’s onto promoting his next completed project, The Exorcist: Martyrs, a film he called “the scariest movie I’ve ever made,” while at Friday’s Blumhouse panel at New York Comic Con.

If you’ve been keeping track, Flanagan’s name has been attached to the iconic horror franchise, which began in 1973 and is based on the William Peter Blatty novel of the same name. Since Linda Blair terrified audiences as the demon-possessed young girl, Regan MacNeil, the movie series expanded. There have been sequels, a prequel and even a short-lived TV show.

			

More from CNET

In 2023, David Gordon Green attempted to reboot the franchise with The Exorcist: The Believer. Now, it’s Flanagan’s turn.

The Exorcist: Martyrs gives a new spin on the Exorcist canon and injects a Minderhunter-style serial killer narrative element into the mix. If you watched the TV series I mentioned above, you’ll notice a similar procedural vibe in the brand-new trailer that dropped during the panel. And if you’re an Exorcist III stan, I’m sure you’ll be happy with the just released clip, as it’s got that similar brooding feeling here.

The Exorcist: Martyrs stars Scarlett Johansson as an NYPD detective tracking a serial killer named Father Sunday (John Leguizamo), who uses Catholic iconography in his kills. Chiwetel Ejiofor, fresh out of The Backrooms, also stars in the film, opposite Laurence Fishburne, Sasha Calle and Jacobi Jupe.

If you’ve been yearning for the Mike Flanagan era of Oculus and The Haunting of Hill House, The Exorcist: Martyrs feels like the filmmaker is back in his terrifying groove. While I’m still waiting for his adaptation of Stephen King’s The Dark Tower to see the light of day, this will have to do.

The Exorcist: Martyrs premieres in theaters on Friday, March 12, 2027.

fullText:
The first two episodes of “Small Prophets” are now available to stream on Apple TV, following a wave of glowing reviews for the British comedy series. Watch the trailer below.

’Small Prophets’ now streaming on Apple TV

Earlier today, my colleague Ryan covered the raving reviews for “Small Prophets,” a British comedy series Apple TV acquired for international distribution earlier this year.

He works in a DIY store, visits his dad Brian (Sir Michael Palin) and hopes for Clea to return. One day Brian shares an old recipe involving rainwater, horse manure and more than a little alchemy. Michael gets help from his young coworker Kacey (Lauren Patel), an unlikely friendship that blossoms partly (but not wholly) through their mutual dislike of store manager Gordon (Mackenzie Crook). title: Dawn Myers is making it easier to style, detangle, and care for curly hair
snippet: Richualist is one of TechCrunch's Battlefield 200 Companies!
fullText:
Normally, Dawn Myers wears her hair up in a big old afro, and anyone with an afro can attest that wash days — the routine of washing and styling textured hair — are often tedious. They take a lot of detangling, product, styling, and, well, time. 

“I was watching ‘Shark Tank,’ and there was another curly girl idea,” she recalled of a day around eight years ago, when a pitch for a hair product aired. She started thinking about all the hair tools on the market, like blow dryers and curling irons, “things that straighten and change the chemistry of our naturally curly hair,” she told TechCrunch, adding that it takes around an hour and 20 minutes to wash and style her own hair. 

None of those tools help with that, and for Myers, it highlighted a gap that has always existed in the beauty hardware space — a lack of tooling for textured hair. It’s a space that’s complex, expensive, and just overlooked. 

“If you think back to slavery, we were mandated to cover our hair. That’s where do-rags come from. You had to cover your hair. Why? Because our hair was seen as ugly and unkempt and unacceptable,” she said. Later came hot combs, chemical relaxers, and flat irons, all of which straighten textured hair. “It’s only been the past 15 years or so where women of color and Black women in particular and, quite frankly, white women as well have really felt comfortable exposing their naturally curly hair and really just embracing it.” 

Soon after that episode aired, she whipped out a legal pad and sketched out a business idea, then went to Ace Hardware and CVS and put together a “Frankenstein-looking prototype.”

Her idea eventually became the company Richualist, which is known for its product Mint, a hair tool that helps detangle, condition, gel, and style in a single stroke using refillable product pods. It even has warming technology to gently heat the product before it’s applied. 

“We get that styling time down to about seven to 10 minutes,” she said. “It’s a massive game changer for the customer really stressed out by wash day.” She said her product, which also comes in travel size, helps make hair a bit healthier, reducing shedding and breakage by up to 70% since people no longer need to tug endlessly on their strands as they wash and style. 

She built it with the materials science company Dow, after an early prototype caught the company’s attention during a startup accelerator program. “It just so happens that Dow had identified this white space recently as well, and they were starting a textured hair care unit,” she said. “So they ended up collaborating with us and giving us a lot of engineering help and manufacturing guidance.” 

Image Credits:Richualist

Even though she eventually became one of the first 100 Black women to raise more than $1 million in venture funding, the early days were rough. “It’s really impossible to get hardware funded,” she continued. “It’s even more impossible to get it funded when we’re talking about such a niche problem.” 

She recalled the early meetings with executives in the beauty industry. “There are no people who look like me in those R&D suites.” In fact, she said, when she described wash days, “these people didn’t know what a wash day was. They didn’t understand that there’s this whole process that their customers have to go through.” She would tell them how painful and arduous the process is. “And the powers that be, up until this point, did not know,” she continued. “Even the bonds in our hair are totally different than other technology types. We really do need bespoke technology.” 

Myers sold her home and liquidated her 401(k) retirement account to fund the initial development of this product. “That was a crazy bet, but it paid off,” she said. “We were able to get about $1.4 million in the door to commercialize the product and just validate it.” Overall, it took about five years of development to get the product to “a place where it made sense to the customer,” she said, adding that her team also had to conduct their own research in the space since what they needed — like how much product the average person with textured hair uses — didn’t yet exist.

Then, in 2022, just as she was about to expand and go to market, she was diagnosed with stage three colorectal cancer. “We ended up closing our round while I was still going through treatment,” she recalled, saying the round took “forever” to close. She remembers sitting in the chemo chair at Johns Hopkins, on her laptop, trying to close deals. She applied to “Shark Tank” in 2023 and appeared on the show later that year, though the episode aired in 2024. “I was still wearing a binder around my abdomen [a compression wrap] under the dress I wore for my ‘Shark Tank’ experience,” she said.

She ended up nabbing a deal from investor Mark Cuban and serial entrepreneur Emma Grede, which helped her formally launch the product. Grede then helped it expand into Ulta’s online website earlier this year. 

“We’re actually about to market ourselves as sold out,” she said, adding that the company is mapping out ways to expand further. 

Her company was picked as one of TechCrunch’s Startup Battlefield 200 startups this year, earning a spot at TechCrunch Disrupt, the publication’s annual startup conference, which kicks off this Tuesday. 

When asked how she first heard about Disrupt, she laughed. “I mean, who doesn’t know about Disrupt?” She said she’s bracing herself, as an introvert, for all the people she will meet and conversations she will have.

“But what I am most excited for is textured hair to be sitting on the stage with some of the most sophisticated tech in the space.”

“I was watching ‘Shark Tank,’ and there was another curly girl idea,” she recalled of a day around eight years ago, when a pitch for a hair product aired. title: Google seems to finally understand why it bought Fitbit
snippet: Good morning! Today, I’m searching for Prime Day deals, watching Chris Rock masterfully dodge questions about The Slap, questioning Sam Altman about whether we have to accept “some bad things” to justify AI’s exponential growth, and brushing up on my chess game after many years of neglect. fullText:
Good morning! Today, I’m searching for Prime Day deals, watching Chris Rock masterfully dodge questions about The Slap, questioning Sam Altman about whether we have to accept “some bad things” to justify AI’s exponential growth, and brushing up on my chess game after many years of neglect.

As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

When Google bought Fitbit back in 2019, it wasn’t clear that the brand had a future. 

As many companies are wont to do, Google had good reason to ingest the accessory maker’s IP and set fire to the rest — but that didn’t happen. After a few fallow years, Fitbit became the software powering the Pixel Watch’s health capabilities, and is now shifting once again to working as a standalone hardware brand within Google.

	

After the monumental success of the Fitbit Air in May, the company is poised to release a Charge follow-up called the Edge. The Charge series hasn’t seen a refresh since 2023, and it appears that Google is updating its design and adding a number of app-like features that should bridge the proverbial gap between tracker and smartwatch.

Of course, Google may not have known Fitbit’s true trajectory back in 2019, but it’s arrived at a place that makes sense: Fitbit’s software is now tightly integrated into all of Google’s health-related endeavors, so the brand is pivoting back to hardware where it made its mark originally.

So the question is whether the Edge, or something like it, is the right move. The Air’s success came from its accessible price ($100) and the growing trend of screenless trackers. I wear a Fitbit Air alongside either a smartwatch or a regular one, and that’s its biggest appeal. And people are going to great lengths to hide the diminutive tracker in places most wearables can’t go. 

The Edge, on the other hand, is a traditional fitness tracker with a few tricks up its sleeve. Judging from the leaks, it will offer notifications, Google Maps, music controls, along with Find My Device support. And of course health tracking that, with a Google Health Premium account, includes an AI-powered fitness coach that’s proven its mettle over the past few months.

I doubt the Edge will have the same cultural impact as the Air, but I also see its existence as proof that Google understands why it bought Fitbit in the first place. Now that it’s plumbed the company for all of its wares, Fitbit rises once again where it all started: with cheap hardware that does just enough well to keep users happy.

✉️ Inbox

Google Messages rolls out new long-press menu with partial copying [Updated]. Our long non-copying nightmare is over.

Nvidia Shield TV Pro is now $299 – a $100 price hike seven years after the Android TV box launched. Nvidia almost singlehandedly caused the RAM crisis, so I think the company should be giving these away free, not increasing the price by 50%.

Pixel 10a gets a $100 price hike, now starting at $599. Oof, this one hurts.

Nothing will let you test new products early with its ‘Community Review’ program. This is how OnePlus got such a loyal following, and Carl Pei is doing it again with Nothing.

Gemini app limiting what models free & AI Plus users can access, AI Pro adding Deep Think. It won’t be a popular decision, but it makes sense as Google prepares to widely release Gemini 4 Argon to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic.

Fantastical’s long-awaited Android debut begins today on Googlebook. Flexibits is an Apple-first company, so it’s pretty interesting that it’s bringing Fantastical to Googlebook. I love this app so I’m pretty stoked that it’s going to come to Android proper next year, too.

Welcome to Cc:, where I ask interesting people in the community about what’s making them happy both inside and outside the world of tech. This week, I’m speaking with Myriam Joire (aka. @tnkgrl), a tech & car journalist and host of the Mobile Tech Podcast.

Who are you?

Myriam Joire (aka. @tnkgrl)

What do you do for work?

I’m a tech & car journalist, podcaster, product & media strategy consultant, speaker, and ex-game developer. I host the Mobile Tech Podcast.

What do you do for fun?

Listen to music, take photos, drive.

What is your relationship like with technology these days?

It’s complicated. I still very much love tech, but I strongly dislike the tech industry, tech bros, Silicon Valley’s greed, and the enshittification of tech.

What are three apps you can’t live without?

Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Photos. Sorry I’m boring (I’m not an app person).

What is a gadget that you love right now?

Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro, Google Pixel Watch 5, Oppo Find X9 Ultra, Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8, Dell XPS 13.

How does AI fit into your life right now?

I mostly use Gemini, mostly for work, to brainstorm headlines for SEO, to create short review summaries, to summarize long documents, and to transcribe my podcast. I use AI photo editing tools (from Google/Samsung/Oppo/Xiaomi/Honor/Apple) for minor edits. I also use Auphonic to clean up audio for my podcast when traditional processing falls short.

What’s a recent book you loved, and why?

Tomboy Survival Guide by Ivan Coyote (because I’m a tomboy).

What’s a recent album you loved, and why?

Echoes — Ancient and Modern by Trevor Horn (because it features covers of artists I love, performed by artists I love, with Trevor Horn’s exquisite production work).

What’s a recent TV show you loved, and why?

Star City on Apple TV+ (because I enjoyed For All Mankind and The Man in the High Castle and generally like alternative universe stories).

What’s a recent movie you loved, and why?

Sinners (because of the vampires, non-white protagonists, and impeccable cinematography).

What’s a recent game you loved, and why?

I don’t play games beyond classics like Tetris (shhh, don’t tell anyone!) What kind of ex-game dev am I?

What’s something offline you do every day that brings you joy?

I walk to the coffee shop every morning after I wake up, get my Americano with cream in my own cup, and then sit (preferably outside) and enjoy drinking it while watching people.

This section has some of our favorite stuff from around the internet. Great videos, weird memes, fun reads, recommended apps, whatever. Send us your recommendations!

I’ve been an Ember Mug user for years, despite being told by practically everyone that it’s a waste of money. But I can’t put a price on drinking perfect-temperature coffee on a busy Saturday morning.

The Ember Mug 3 has an upgrade I appreciate more than any other: you can put it in the dishwasher. The 14-ounce mug also lets you set the temperature directly on the mug, and Ember claims over three hours of battery life with the included sliding lid. It’s $150, so it remains an expensive answer to cooling coffee.

If you don’t need the additional battery life and waterproofing over the previous generation, the Ember Mug 2 is down to $100 right now for Prime Big Deal Days.

If you’ve never sat down for a Noclip documentary, you need to set aside a weekend or two to catch up. The studio has covered everything from classics like Half-Life and Dishonored to modern gems like Disco Elysium and Hades.

Now they’re back with a six-part series on Hades II, the first of which is available now. Supergiant Games feels like an anomaly in the gaming industry, a small, tight-knit studio based in San Francisco that makes ambitious, weird games that always seem to sell well. It’s a good news story in an industry that lacks a lot of it right now.

🤑 Action items

It’s Fall Prime Day (also known as Prime Big Deal Days), and I’ve been looking for headphone discounts.

The Nothing Headphone (1) is down to $189, its lowest price ever and a very good deal if you’re looking for great-sounding over-ear headphones. The Nothing (3) earbuds are also down to $99, far below their previous low of $129.

Most of Sony’s high-end headphones are on sale, including the WH-1000XM5s at $198, which matches their lowest price ever. The newer WH-1000XM6s are also down to their lowest price ever at $378, $20 lower than during Prime Day in June. And the WF-1000XM6 earbuds are at $258, also an all-time low. You can also get the same deals from Sony directly, if you’re into that.

Finally, the AirPods Pro 3 are down to $179, which is a great deal on the most popular earbuds on earth.

title: Logitech brings its mouse & keyboard controller to Googlebook, supports Magic Pointer
snippet: Logitech has just launched its Logi Options+ app for Googlebook, bringing support for controlling its keyboard and wireless mice to the Android-based platform. more…
fullText:
Logitech has just launched its Logi Options+ app for Googlebook, bringing support for controlling its keyboard and wireless mice to the Android-based platform.

Previously available on Windows and macOS, Logi Options+ is the app needed to control Logitech peripherals such as the MX Master mouse, various keyboards, and more. This includes adjusting the functions of Logitech’s added buttons and shortcuts, as well as updating firmware on the products.

Logitech does warn that features are “limited” at launch, but there are plenty of supported peripherals including MX Master 4, MX Keys S, Logitech Lift, Pebble Keys 2, and more.

For Logitech mice, this also ensures Googlebook’s Magic Pointer feature works. Logitech says:

	

Pair your supported Logitech device with Googlebook using the Logi Options+ App. Get the best of Gemini with features like Magic Pointer, Circle to search, personalize mouse buttons or keyboard keys, optimize pointing and scrolling experience with Options+, designed specially for your Googlebook.

Logi Options+ for Googlebook is available now via the Google Play Store.

title: These US states just said ‘no’ to Apple Wallet driver’s licenses
snippet: Apple Wallet driver’s licenses keeps expanding to more US states, but two states recently indicated they won’t launch support anytime soon—if at all. more…
fullText:
Apple Wallet driver’s licenses keeps expanding to more US states, but two states recently indicated they won’t launch support anytime soon—if at all.

Florida and Rhode Island won’t be getting Apple Wallet driver’s licenses anytime soon, per key leaders

The number of US states offering Apple Wallet driver’s licenses keeps growing, and we even have a good idea of three states launching support soon.

Plenty of states likely intend to support digital driver’s licenses at some point, and haven’t gotten around to it. But there are two who recently indicated they have no plans to launch support.

Those two states are:

Florida

Rhode Island

Last week, Florida rolled out a brand new driver’s license and ID card. Many states take such occasions to launch digital versions too, but the state made zero announcements around digital ID.

That’s no coincidence, as Governor Ron DeSantis actively opposes the idea of digital driver’s licenses. He posted the following on X last November:

The convenience of a digital drivers license is outweighed by the potential for government to abuse it.  

Not gonna happen in FL.  

No digital ID. https://t.co/YD7J6PtBgR

— Ron DeSantis (@RonDeSantis) November 28, 2025

Florida previously did offer a digital ID but abruptly ended support in 2024. Perhaps the next governor will take a different stance.

In Rhode Island, Walter “Bud” Craddock was on a podcast last week discussing mobile driver’s licenses (“MDL”). Craddock is currently Chair of the American Association of Motor Vehicle Administrators (AAMVA) International Board of Directors.

	

Here’s what he said:

“I want to see more universal adoption or need for an MDL. I had one of my senators approach and try to talk me into doing it. I had to give him the old Heisman move and push him back…the main user right now is TSA. Up until recently, there was no airport in New England area that could accept an MDL. So why would I spend the money in the development of it? And also, I’m looking to do a solution that is across all platforms. Instead of just doing one for Apple or the Google Wallets, I don’t want to replicate and duplicate efforts.”

Like DeSantis, Craddock’s position of leadership is slated to end in the next few months. So depending on his successor’s stance, perhaps Rhode Island could get Apple Wallet driver’s licenses sometime in 2027.

Here’s the full list of US states currently offering Apple Wallet driver’s licenses, and three expected to launch next.

title: Review: Rhinoshield’s iPhone 18 Pro bumper case is minimalist but surprisingly protective
snippet: iPhone bumper cases have been a fan-favorite since the iPhone 4 bumpers, but options these days are few and far between. Rhinoshield offers a decent option for those wanting a minimal case. more…
fullText:
iPhone bumper cases have been a fan-favorite since the iPhone 4 bumpers, but options these days are few and far between. Rhinoshield offers a decent option for those wanting a minimal case.

Apple finally got back into the bumper business with the iPhone Air last year. I was hoping Apple would expand their bumper case to the iPhone 18 Pro (like they did with the clear case and iPhone 11), but unfortunately they did not. In my search for another option, I came across Rhinoshield’s Minimalist Impact Bumper case. 

Key Details

The Impact Bumper Case has a fit similar to most other bumpers, where the lip on the screen is fairly minor, while the lip on the back is a little larger. A unique feature of this case, and one that I quite like, is that it has special supports that keep the camera plateau and lenses off of wherever your phone is resting, which I particularly appreciate considering the aluminum 17 Pro and 18 Pro. This results in a far more protective case than your typical bumper would be. It also eliminates the annoying wobble when using your phone on a flat surface.

The case’s fit, however, is not quite what I was hoping for. It’s somewhat loose, and you can easily bend the edges outward, and I do wonder if over time they may end up getting stretched out. I don’t think the phone flying out of the case when dropped will be an issue though (and I have unintentionally tested that). That said, the material of the entire case is a hard plastic rather than rubber, so hopefully it will be fine in the long run. Rhinoshield says that it is made entirely of just one material, and is therefore 100% recyclable.

The case comes in three colors, which are matched to the iPhone 18 Pro colors: white, blue, and black (sorry Burgundy fans). The blue, which is what I have, is close to Glacier but not perfect. 

Downsides

There are some downsides, however. My primary gripe with the case is that the buttons can be hard to press. For some reason they went with a nearly flush design, and the way that the buttons are designed makes them mushy. 

The material choice as a whole may be a downside. To me, it feels cheaper than the likes of Apple’s iPhone Air bumper, but some may end up preferring it. I certainly prefer it to the materials of a typical TPU/rubber clear case. The material and loose design also seem to attract pocket dust.

If you use Apple’s Wrist Strap or Crossbody Strap, be aware that this case does not have the required loop connection points. 

Conclusion

The Rhinoshield bumper is definitely not perfect, and I still hope that Apple will extend their bumpers to other iPhones. In the end though, I have decided to keep the case, for one primary reason: it lets me have a near-caseless experience without worry of the fragile aluminum getting chipped or dented. As far as I can tell, the bumper case is usually only available from their own website, so the price of about $30 matches the price of Apple’s ($39) after shipping. You can get the Rhinoshield Minimalist Impact Bumper case here. (Occasionally, an Amazon listing will pop up, so you can give that a try as well.)

title: Googlebooks don’t have the same web app or Linux app support as Chromebooks
snippet: Googlebooks don’t have the same level of web app support as Chromebooks, as only “compliant” apps can be installed, and that’s not the only regression from ChromeOS, as Linux apps don’t work in the same way either. more…
fullText:
Googlebooks don’t have the same level of web app support as Chromebooks, as only “compliant” apps can be installed, and that’s not the only regression from ChromeOS, as Linux apps don’t work in the same way either.

Googlebooks rely on Android apps and web apps for virtually all core functionality, with the Play Store actively directing users to which app is the most ideal on the platform. 

As it turns out, though, support for Progressive Web Apps on Googlebook isn’t quite at the same level as Chromebook. While most PWAs we’ve tried so far are easily installed, we ran into an issue installing the Slack PWA. Google, in a statement today, confirmed this is because Slack is not a “compliant” PWA, with Chromebooks instead relying on “manual installation.” It’s unclear what differs regarding Slack’s PWA — it functions just fine on other platforms such as Windows and ChromeOS — but it can’t be installed on Googlebook or Android devices.

Google says:

	

Installing PWAs is fully supported on Googlebooks. But, the Slack web app isn’t a compliant PWA. Chrome on ChromeOS allows manual installation even though it’s not a PWA. This capability will also be coming to Chrome on Googlebooks soon.

This mirrors another regression in app support compared to Chromebooks.

Googlebooks also, at least for now, lack the same level of Linux app support.

Chromebooks started adding support for installing Linux apps way back in 2018 and, after a few years in development, it became a secret super power of Google’s platform. Linux app support on Chromebook allowed users to bridge the app gap with the ability to install full desktop apps via Linux ports and, while it wasn’t the easiest process, it got the job done.

Googlebooks are in a very different state.

There’s little to no documentation around Linux apps on Googlebook right now, with Google’s only page on the matter describing how you can use the Terminal app to access a Debian command line interface. Google says:

You can use the Terminal app to access a powerful Debian Linux command-line environment directly on your Googlebook. You can install and run developer tools, code environments, and access other Linux applications. It expands your device’s capabilities for advanced tasks and software development.

But installing apps via this portal doesn’t put them within easy reach of the end user. It’s a far cry from Chromebook’s support, which placed most apps within the app drawer once they were installed. 

	

Google says that it’s possible to run apps, but that GUI apps “aren’t the main focus” of the Linux environment on Googlebook:

Just wanted to confirm that yes, there will be a Terminal app available on Googlebook out of the box, and yes it lets you run a Debian Linux environment on your device.

Also yes, you CAN run Linux GUI apps in this environment, but note that for this initial release of Googlebook, GUI apps aren’t the main focus. We’ll have more to share soon on the Terminal app!

One Linux user far more experienced than myself who dug into how Googlebook supports Linux apps, detailing that they show up in a single Terminal display window without their own Android windows or taskbar items. Another user saw the same behavior and noted reliability issues with GIMP, a popular photo editing app for Linux.

As mentioned, there’s no documentation yet on how to get Linux GUI apps running on Googlebook, so this is not functionality for the “average Joe” — not to say Linux apps on Chromebook were either, but it’s certainly odd to see that this has regressed in functionality rather than expanded.

title: Pixel 11 series still not on Android 17 QPR1 with October update
snippet: With yesterday’s October 2026 update, the Pixel 11 series is not yet running Android 17 QPR1. more…
fullText:
With yesterday’s October 2026 update, the Pixel 11 series is not yet running Android 17 QPR1.

The Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold launched in August with the base Android 17 release. In September, the Pixel 11 series received two early updates that presumably addressed issues that emerged since launch. 

	

Later in the month, Google rolled out QPR1 to all other devices. Visual changes in the quarterly release include system blur for the volume slider and power menu, while there’s an updated system media player that gets narrower when other apps are available. The Mobile Data Quick Settings Tile gets a time-saving “Don’t ask me again” toggle, while there’s now a Keyboard QS Tile.

Meanwhile, the Pixel 11 series did not get the initial Android 17 QPR2 Beta 6 release and had to wait a few days for Beta 6.1, which introduced HiLight support for message notifications. It did get the 17 QPR3 Beta without issue a few days later. 

	

This week’s October release does contain fixes for the Pixel 11:

Fix for issue causing the virtual keyboard to occasionally not appear when interacting with search input fields*[1]

Fix for issue occasionally causing captured photos or recorded videos to save in the incorrect orientation*[3]

It’s unlikely that we’ll get a second October release, with all eyes on November. With QPR2 just a month away at that point, Google might wait for December to align all the devices.
